1 College Scorecard

The data folder contains college_scorecard_extract_2025-11-17_413.csv, a subset of data in the College Scorecard as of November 17, 2025. This data set contains information on undergraduate college cohorts in the United States. The data dictionary is in the data folder. The variables include:

  • ADM_RATE: The Admission Rate
  • AGE_ENTRY: Average age of entry
  • AVGFACSAL: Average faculty salary per Month
  • CITY: City
  • CONTROL: Ownership-Public or Private: 1=‘Public Institution’, 2=‘Private nonprofit Institution’, 3=‘Private for-profit institution’, -3=‘not available’;
  • COSTT4_A: Average cost of attendance (academic year institutions)
  • ENDOWBEGIN: Endowment at the beginning of the fiscal year.
  • FEMALE: Percentage of female students
  • FIRSTGEN: Share of first-generation students
  • GRAD_DEBT_MDN: The median debt for students who have completed
  • HBCU: Flag for Historically Black College and University, 1 is HBCU-Yes
  • HSI: Flag for Hispanic-serving institution
  • ICLEVEL: Level of institution (1 = 4-year, 2 = 2-year, 3 = less than 2-year).
  • INSTNM: Institution name
  • INSTURL: URL for institution’s homepage
  • MD_EARN_WNE_P10: Median earnings of students working and not enrolled 10 years after entry.
  • NANTI: Flag for Native American non-tribal institution
  • OPEID: Identifier for the colleges. A “main campus” has an 8-digit OPE ID that starts with 0 and ends with 00; digits 2 through 6 are referred to as the “root.” Separate reporting entities in IPEDS are referred to as “institutions” and may include Branch campuses and additional locations which share the root.
  • PCIP13: Percentage of degrees awarded in Education.
  • PCIP14: Percentage of degrees awarded in Engineering.
  • PCIP27: Percentage of degrees awarded in Mathematics And Statistics.
  • PCIP52: Percentage of degrees awarded in Business, Management, Marketing, And Related Support Services.
  • PCTPELL: Percentage of undergraduates who receive a Pell Grant
  • PFTFAC: Proportion of faculty that is full-time
  • PREDDEG: Predominant undergraduate degree awarded. 0 Not classified, 1 Predominantly certificate-degree granting, 2 Predominantly associate’s-degree granting, 3 Predominantly bachelor’s-degree granting, 4 Entirely graduate-degree granting”
  • RELAFFIL: Religious affiliation of the institution
  • SAT_AVE: Average SAT equivalent score of students admitted.
  • SCH_DEG: Predominant degree awarded (recoded 0s and 4s)
  • STABBR: State postal code
  • UGDS: Enrollment of undergraduate certificate/degree-seeking students
  • UGDS_MEN: Percent of male undergraduates
  • UGDS_WOMEN: Percent of female undergraduates
  • Total share of enrollment of undergraduate degree-seeking students who are
    • UGDS_2MOR: Two or more races
    • UGDS_AIAN: American Indian/Alaska Native
    • UGDS_API: Asian/Pacific Islander. All NA so not used.
    • UGDS_ASIAN: Asian
    • UGDS_BLACK: Black
    • UGDS_BLACKNH: Black non-Hispanic. All NA so not used.
    • UGDS_HISP: Hispanic undergraduates
    • UGDS_NHPI: Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander
    • UGDS_UNKN: Unknown
    • UGDS_NRA: Non-resident Alien
    • UGDS_WHITE: White
  • DATE: Date of the data set

4. How is average faculty salary associated with the median earnings of working students ten years after initial enrollment? Create the plot per the steps in part a, then answer parts b, c, and d as text.

  1. Remove the NA values for just the variables of interest and use {ggplot2} to create a scatter plot plot to assess for a relationship (with AVGFACSAL as the explanatory X variable).
  • Use an argument of geom_point() to reduce over-plotting by decreasing opacity of the points.
  • Add the default smoother with se = FALSE.
  • Facet on ICLEVEL.
  1. Interpret the plots about the potential relationships.
  2. Why did geom_smooth() chose the mgcv::gam() smoothing method instead of the default stats::loess()?
  3. Why is there no ICLEVEL 3 plot, or, if there is a plot, why is there no data in the ICLEVEL 3 plot?

Now answer parts e though h.

  1. Use lm() to run a linear model of the relationship for only those schools with ICLEVEL 1 and save the results.

  2. Use summary() on the results.

  3. Interpret the results of the model based on the coefficient for AVGFACSAL and the model \(p\)-value and adjusted \(r\)-squared value.

  4. Given the adjusted \(r\)-squared value, what do you recommend to try to better predict average earnings of working students ten years after initial enrollment at ICLEVEL 1 schools?

  • Use ggthemes::theme_fivethirtyeight().
  • Use a {knitr} code chunk option to set the figure width at 6. https://quarto.org/docs/computations/execution-options.html#figure-options

  1. Interpret the plot to answer the question.

  2. Use aov() to test if all of the institution levels have the same true mean of logged median earnings of working students ten years after enrollment.

  2. What are the ethical implications of using either the linear smoother or the non-linear smoother in these plots to “prove a point”? Which would you recommend and why?

7. How do colleges rank based on their ratio of Student Debt at graduation to the Annual Cost to Attend. Call it the Debt/Cost Ratio (DCR). Answer the question in the following steps.

  1. Filter the data to only ICLEVEL 1 schools with no NAs for COSTT4_A or GRAD_DEBT_MDN.
  • Remove any satellite campuses using filter(str_detect(OPEID, "......00")). That should leave 1,678 rows.

  1. Add a variable called DCR based on the ratio of median debt at graduation to the Average cost of attendance (academic year institutions) which is then rounded to 2 decimal places.

  2. Use a {dplyr} integer ranking function to compute a ranking based on DCR.

  • Break any ties using the smallest value and leaving a gap to the next untied DCR such that if two schools are tied for 4th, they are each ranked 4th and the next school is ranked 6th. This is similar to many sports rankings.
  1. Identify the just top 5 best schools (lowest DCR should be rank value 1). Then identify the just he bottom 5 worst schools (largest DCR should have largest rank number).
  • Show only the rank, name, DCR, cost to attend, median debt at graduation, and the median earnings 10 years after enrollment.

  1. What is American University’s rank and DCR? Show only the rank, name, DCR, cost to attend, median debt at graduation, and median earnings 10 years after enrollment.

2 World Bank Data

The World Bank provides loans to countries with the goal of reducing poverty. The data frames in the data folder were taken from the public data repositories of the World Bank Group DataBank. The fertility, life expectancy, and population data are from its World Development Indicators (WDI) as of 1 August 2025.

  • WB_Country_classification_2025_07_02.xlsx: Contains information on the countries in the data set. The “List of Economies” tab includes totals for the regions (sets of countries) and the world. Source is World Bank Country and Lending Groups. The variables are:
    • Economy: The full name of the country or region.
    • Code: A three-letter code for the country. Note: not all rows are countries; there are rows for the regions and for the world which may confuse totals if not excluded.
    • Region: The region of the country. Note: The Economy variable includes observations for defined groups of countries, such as regions, and for the world. These have the value NA for Region.
    • Income Group: Either "High income", "Upper middle income", "Lower middle income", or "Low income".
    • Lending Category: IDA (International Development Association): Low-income countries eligible for concessional financing. Blend: Countries eligible for both IDA and International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) assistance. IBRD (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development): Middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries.

The WB_WDI_data_25_08_21.csv file has World Development Indicators for each economy and year for

  • Fertility rate in total births per woman.
  • Life expectancy at birth in years .
  • Total population in number of people based on the de facto definition which counts all residents regardless of legal status or citizenship. The values shown are mid-year estimates.

1. Use a relative path and {readxl) or {readr} functions to load each of these files into its own tibble so we only have the data for individual countries, not regions or the world.

  • Use an argument of the function that reads the data to ensure there is a maximum of 219 rows for the country data and a maximum of 651 rows for the WDI data.
    • Note: the two packages use the same name for the argument but readr functions do not count header rows as they check for them first, before reading the data and read_xlsx functions do count them as they only look for header rows after reading in the data.
  • Note: Some countries have NA or “..” for missing data.
  • Be sure to look at the data after loading to ensure it loaded as expected, without problems (e.g., numeric data mistakenly being read in as character), and fix any problems using function arguments.

Use glimpse() to show a maximum of 10 columns of data for each tibble.

2. Use anti_join() to show which codes are in the country data but not in the WDI data. - Then use anti_join() to show which country codes are in WDI data but not in the country data.
- Note: Per the general instructions, you cannot rename variables.

You should have 14,075 rows and 6 columns of which the last 4 are all type double.

  • Now shorten the names of the indicator columns. Convert to snake case, e.g., lower case with “_” not ” “.
  • Use set_seed(123) and then show a random sample of 10 rows.
